newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia likely to put off VAT for a year - Deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Croatia likely to put off VAT for a year - Deputy PM.

text.p: Croatia will probably put off introduction of value added tax (VAT) for a year but the date must be set by law, Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro said on Friday.
"For technical reasons and because it is unusual to apply a new tax in the middle of the year, I hope the parliament will postpone VAT's introduction until January 1, 1998," Skegro told reporters.
VAT was due to be launched as a finale to a comprehensive fiscal reform at a rate of 22 percent from next year to replace the current turnover tax, which is higher.
But under pressure from various social groups and in view of the coming election, the ruling party HDZ last week instructed the government to postpone it.
While Croatia's stimulating exports, that were to be exempt from the new levy, VAT would have increased the price of basic consumables such as bread which are not taxed now.
Government officials have repeatedly vowed to compensate for its effects on the poorest citizens by income tax relief and increased welfare subsidies.

However, officials in favour of its introduction from this coming January despite loud criticism, partly also from uninformed tax payers, were largely outnumbered, Skegro said. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
